text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: Do weekly automated scans of all prompts using exact string matching. This catches hard-coded values and direct references that semantic scans miss, ensuring no prompt drifts out of sync. Trade-off: exact matching can’t detect paraphrased or rephrased prompts, so we accept missing some subtle changes to avoid false positives from semantic drift.

name: Gauge
text: Exact string matching risks overlooking critical variations in prompts, which can lead to inconsistencies and errors over time. A better alternative is to implement hybrid scanning, which combines exact matching with semantic analysis. This approach detects a wider range of changes, including paraphrased prompts, and ensures better alignment while still maintaining manageable performance levels. Settling the argument would require evidence of reduced errors in real-world scenarios using hybrid scanning versus relying solely on exact matches.
